subject: Private Offer: usage-anchor harmonization & channel uplift path
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <procurement@orchidcloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer unit metrics + reseller uplift question

Hi Irene,

We're working through the procurement checklist for the Private Offer you provided and have two related items blocking final sign-off:

1) Usage metric harmonization — your draft PO currently quotes both ‘vCPU‑hours’ and ‘inference tokens’ across SKUs. Our billing runs on a monthly vCPU-hour baseline for model serving (we shape commitments around that). Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a vCPU-hour anchoring for the committed units (with token-based overage) and share a short worked example?

2) Channel uplift / reseller pass-through — our reseller requires a 3% uplift to cover distributor fees. We need to understand how that uplift will appear on your invoices and whether it changes net revenue calculations for rebate/commitment tiers.

If you can loop in the finance/ops lead and a short sample of how the PO/invoice would look, we can move to internal approval.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of Procurement
Orchid Cloud

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer unit metrics + reseller uplift question

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear note. Looping Jordan (deal lead) and Ben (finance) to align on the mapping and invoice flow. Quick responses inline: 

1) vCPU anchoring: We can anchor the committed capacity on vCPU-hours for a single serving profile (e.g., m40 inference profile). For models/run‑time variance we'll expose token-based overage lines. Jordan will propose the SKU mapping and a sample monthly invoice that shows committed vCPU consumption, overage tokens, and a single net line with uplift applied.

2) Reseller uplift: We can represent the 3% uplift as a surcharge line on the invoice that is visually separated from Redwood list price and is treated as pass-through. We need confirmation on whether Orchid expects Redwood to remit any of that uplift to a third party or whether Orchid will handle pass-through payments. Ben — can you confirm the accounting treatment and whether the uplift affects list-price based commit bands?

Next step: Jordan will attach a draft SKU mapping + PO example today; Ben will advise on the netting. If that looks ok we can produce an updated PO for signature.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer unit metrics + reseller uplift question

Aisha / Irene — attaching a first pass at SKU mapping and a short worked example. Key points: 

- We create a committed SKU 1 (vCPU-anchor) for ‘serving-profile-m40’ with a monthly committed vCPU‑hours quantity. 
- Overage SKU 2 will be token-metered at the model's inference token rate.
- The invoice will show: List price (committed), Overage charges (tokens), Reseller uplift (3% surcharge) as a separate line. Net revenue used for commit-bands will be computed before the surcharge (i.e., surcharge treated as pass-through).

I've also included a simple CSV pricing_workback.csv that demonstrates month-to-month treatment for a sample 1000 vCPU‑hours commit. See row examples. 

Ben/Naomi — please flag if the netting approach above causes any recognition or rebate issues.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer unit metrics + reseller uplift question

Jordan / Irene — quick finance note from my side:

- Treating the 3% as an explicit surcharge line that is excluded from list-price-based commit calculations is workable. That means commit tiers and rebate calculations use Redwood list price and Overage lines only.
- For revenue recognition we will record the surcharge as pass-through liability and not Redwood service revenue; this keeps commission & rebate math clean.
- One operational ask: we need Orchid to confirm billing contact and whether the distributor expects Redwood to issue a separate invoice to them. If Orchid prefers the uplift to be remitted by Redwood to a named distributor, we will need a signed reseller agreement and the distributor’s billing tax info.

I'll leave a short note in HubSpot and attach the recommended PO language for the invoice lines.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — the SKU mapping and worked example look good. A few clarifications before we finalize: 

1) Invoice flow: Orchid prefers a single invoice from Redwood to Orchid that includes a clearly labeled ‘Reseller surcharge’ line. Orchid will handle downstream payments to our distributor, so Redwood does not need to remit the uplift.

2) Tax/treatment: Our finance team needs the surcharge to be identified separately for tax reporting; please ensure the PO language and invoice template show the surcharge as a distinct taxable/non-taxable line (we will provide our tax guidance if needed).

3) Timing: If you can provide the updated PO with wording reflecting the surcharge-as-pass-through and the sample invoice, we can get internal procurement sign-off next week.
